sections.content: How many people are "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers"?

18,580 people

were counted on the census as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Furniture makers and other craft woodworkers make, repair and restore wooden furniture, decorative objects and other crafted pieces of woodwork.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" there were more men than women (86.2% compared with 13.8%).

This means "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 86.2% and women made up 13.8% of "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" included:

  • process operatives (other)
  • sports players
  • civil engineers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" was 16 to 19 years.

We can look at who worked as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "furniture makers and other craft woodworkers", 10.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (74.3% compared with 25.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (57%) than self-employed (43%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kirklees, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
